primary.key: When a reconciliation is effected (between two parties) after a great animosity, there is sure to be a grudge remaining (in the mind of the one who was wrong).
primary.s: The chapter opens on this difficulty before turning to the sage’s half of the record; Wang Bi, on chapter 79, reads the animosity as born of an agreement not clearly settled, and the grudge as a wound that reconciling by virtue does not heal.
primary.src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 79, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

basis.words: 不明理其契，以致大怨已至。而德和之，其傷不復，故有餘怨也。
basis.gloss: Failing to settle the terms of one’s agreement clearly brings it about that great resentment has come; and though virtue then reconciles it, the wound is not restored, and so resentment remains.

standby.key: In the Way of Heaven, there is no partiality of love; it is always on the side of the good man.
standby.s: Closing a chapter on the sage who presses no claim, the verse turns to Heaven; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 79, reads Heaven as holding none near or far, and the good man it favours as the one who keeps to the tally.
standby.src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 79, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 1552800 (2019)

basis.words: 有德之君，司察契信而已。…天道無有親疏，唯與善人，則與司契者也。
basis.gloss: The ruler who has virtue attends only to the good faith of the tally, nothing more. … The Way of Heaven holds none near and none far; it gives only to good men, that is, to those who keep to the tally.

primary.key: Though they had boats and carriages, they should have no occasion to ride in them; though they had buff coats and sharp weapons, they should have no occasion to don or use them.
primary.s: Picturing a little state of few people, the chapter turns to travel and arms; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 80, reads the idle boats as stillness and non-action, fond of no pleasure trips, and the idle arms as no resentment anywhere under Heaven.
primary.src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 80, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 1552800 (2019)

basis.words: 清靜無為，不作煩華，不好出入遊娛也。…無怨惡於天下。
basis.gloss: Clear and still, not acting, making no troublesome show, not fond of going out and about for travel and amusement. … No resentment or hatred anywhere under Heaven.

standby.key: In a little state with a small population, I would so order it, that, though there were individuals with the abilities of ten or a hundred men, there should be no employment of them; I would make the people, while looking on death as a grievous thing, yet not remove elsewhere (to avoid it).
standby.s: The chapter opens with the speaker imagining how he would govern; Wang Bi, on chapter 80, reads the little state as an example: if even a small state of few people can be turned back to antiquity, how much more a large, populous one.
standby.src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 80, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

basis.words: 國既小，民又寡，尚可使反古，況國大民眾乎？故舉小國而言也。
basis.gloss: The state being small and its people few, it can still be made to return to antiquity; how much more a state that is large, with many people. So the text takes the small state to speak of.

primary.key: The sage does not accumulate (for himself). The more that he expends for others, the more does he possess of his own; the more that he gives to others, the more does he have himself.
primary.s: The last chapter, after sayings on speech and knowing, turns here to the sage; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 81, reads him as storing up virtue, not wealth: his virtue grows as he spreads it, his wealth as he gives it away.
primary.src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 81, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 1552800 (2019)

basis.words: 聖人積德不積財，有德以教愚，有財以與貧也。…既以為人施設德化，己愈有德。…既以財賄布施與人，而財益多
basis.gloss: The sage stores up virtue and does not store up wealth: having virtue, he teaches the ignorant; having wealth, he gives to the poor. … Having spread the transforming work of virtue for others, he himself has the more virtue. … Having given his goods and wealth away to others, his wealth grows the more.

standby.key: The sage does not accumulate (for himself). The more that he expends for others, the more does he possess of his own; the more that he gives to others, the more does he have himself.
standby.s: Between sayings on speech and on Heaven’s Way, the last chapter turns to the sage; Wang Bi, on chapter 81, reads him as free of self-interest, siding only with the good, and his having more as things honouring him and turning to him.
standby.src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 81, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

basis.words: 無私自有，唯善是與，任物而已。…物所尊也。…物所歸也。
basis.gloss: Free of self-interest, he has of himself; he sides only with the good; he leaves things to themselves, nothing more. … He is the one things honour. … He is the one things turn to.
